_meta.purpose: Internal research registry for Getszy Agent Factory open-source capability integration.
_meta.rule: Verify official repo + owner + license before any integration. Ambiguous identity => NEEDS_REVIEW, do not integrate. Open source != commercially compatible. Prefer learning architecture/patterns over copying source; for adapted/direct reuse, preserve license + attribution.
_meta.commit_pinning: Commits are intentionally null here — pin the exact SHA at the integration step (Integration Strategy #2), not at research time. Never fabricate a SHA.
_meta.security_invariant: Every external skill/tool/service is untrusted input and MUST route through the existing Factory security layer: adapter -> agent_guard -> permission check -> sandbox/tool -> execute -> verification. No external capability may bypass agent_guard, approval gates, sandbox, or audit logging.

candidates.name: browser-use
candidates.license_note: Repo page reports MIT; one search snippet claimed AGPL-3.0. DISCREPANCY — re-read LICENSE at the pinned commit before any source reuse.
candidates.resource_cost: Python + a browser engine (Chromium). Non-trivial RAM.
candidates.rationale: playwright-mcp (Apache-2.0, accessibility-tree, no vision model) is the cleaner, lighter fill for Getszy browser/E2E. Learn browser-use's plan/observe loop; do not vendor.

candidates.name: OpenViking
candidates.license_note: Main project AGPL-3.0 (some components e.g. CLI/examples Apache-2.0). AGPL is a strong copyleft/network-copyleft risk for a proprietary commercial core.
candidates.capability: Self-evolving context database unifying agent memory + knowledge RAG + skills as a virtual filesystem (viking://), with tiered L0/L1/L2 on-demand context loading and retrieval trajectories.
rejected_patterns: vendoring AGPL source into proprietary core
candidates.resource_cost: Full context DB service; heavier than needed on a constrained VPS.
candidates.rationale: Per master directive: architectural reference only. Do NOT vendor AGPL into Getszy core. Adopt the tiered-retrieval + provenance IDEAS in a Getszy-native memory abstraction. Only reconsider as an ISOLATED external service after explicit legal review.

candidates.name: codebase-memory-mcp
candidates.license_note: MIT confirmed via community fork description (win4r/codebase-memory-mcp-pro: 'Community fork of DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp (MIT)'). Verify LICENSE at pin.
candidates.capability: Pure-C MCP server; indexes a codebase into a persistent knowledge graph (functions, classes, call chains, HTTP routes, cross-service links) via tree-sitter; single static binary, sub-ms structural queries.
useful_patterns: token-cheap structural queries vs dumping files
candidates.resource_cost: Single static binary, low RAM. Attractive for a constrained VPS.
candidates.rationale: Optional external MCP service behind a Factory adapter (guard-gated, read-only over the repo). Alternative: LEARN the graph schema and build a lightweight native Python repo-map. Fills the real 'no structural codebase intelligence' gap.

candidates.name: agency-swarm
candidates.capability: Multi-agent orchestration; typed specialist agents with roles, instructions, and tool sets; communication flows.
rejected_patterns: adopting its runtime/orchestration (Getszy already has agent_delegation with guardrails)
candidates.rationale: Getszy already has a stronger, guard-integrated delegation runtime. Borrow the role/tool-policy/output-contract SHAPE to build a native Specialist Role Registry; do not adopt the framework.

candidates.name: mem0
candidates.capability: Memory layer (bolt-on) for agents: add/search/update memories across sessions with storage+retrieval.
useful_patterns: memory as add/search/get facade decoupled from agent
candidates.resource_cost: Optional; can run with lightweight backends.
candidates.rationale: Apache-2.0 is commercially safe. Adapt the add/search/scope facade shape into the Getszy-native Memory Interface. Optional future mem0 adapter behind the interface; Factory must work without it (fail closed).

candidates.name: Letta (formerly MemGPT)
candidates.capability: Stateful agent runtime with OS-inspired memory management (memory blocks, context paging, self-editing memory).
candidates.rationale: Learn the memory-block + context-paging concepts for the native Memory Interface's compression/progressive-retrieval. Do not adopt the runtime.

candidates.name: Composio
candidates.capability: Unified API/tool layer: 1000+ connectors, managed OAuth, tool search, sandboxed workbench.
rejected_patterns: installing the full platform + 1000 connectors on a constrained VPS
managed-OAuth surface expanding the trust boundary
candidates.rationale: MIT-safe but too heavy to vendor. Learn the tool-schema/registry pattern for a native unified tool registry (schema->permission-class->execute->evidence->audit). Selected connectors could later be ISOLATED behind adapters if truly needed.

candidates.name: playwright-mcp
candidates.capability: MCP server for browser automation via Playwright's accessibility tree (no vision model needed); tools like browser_navigate/click/type/snapshot.
candidates.resource_cost: Node + Playwright browser (Chromium). Moderate RAM; isolate/lazy-start.
candidates.rationale: Preferred browser fill. Run as an isolated MCP service behind a Factory adapter -> guard -> isolated browser session. plan->act->observe->verify->evidence; no success without observable evidence.

candidates.name: playwright
useful_patterns: deterministic E2E tests as verification evidence
candidates.rationale: Apache-2.0. Use as the E2E test runner powering the browser-verification harness; artifacts become repair-loop evidence.

candidates.name: anthropics/skills
candidates.license_note: Mixed: code skills Apache-2.0; document skills are source-available reference only. Do not treat the whole repo as one license.
candidates.capability: Reference implementation of the Agent Skills format (SKILL.md + scripts/resources, progressive disclosure).
rejected_patterns: copying source-available document skills into a commercial product
candidates.rationale: Learn the SKILL.md registry pattern to build a native Getszy Skill Registry (declarative capability, execution stays in Factory). Per-skill: Apache-2.0 code skills may be ADAPTED with attribution; document skills are LEARN_ONLY.

candidates.name: Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills (3rd-party)
candidates.owner_note: Owner is 'mukul975', NOT Anthropic. The name 'Anthropic cybersecurity skills' is misleading — this is a community catalog, not an official Anthropic release.
candidates.capability: Large catalog of cybersecurity skills mapped to MITRE ATT&CK / NIST CSF / ATLAS / D3FEND.
rejected_patterns: trusting unvetted third-party security scripts as executable skills
candidates.rationale: Name/provenance ambiguity + security-sensitive content from an unofficial owner. Do not integrate as executable skills without file-by-file audit. May LEARN the recon->hunt->validate->report taxonomy.

candidates.name: MoneyPrinterTurbo
candidates.capability: One-click short-video generation (script -> search terms -> stock clips -> TTS -> subtitles -> FFmpeg assembly).
rejected_patterns: making it part of Agent Factory core
candidates.resource_cost: FFmpeg + media; Getszy already has this (video_factory).
candidates.rationale: Per directive: NOT Factory core. Getszy's video_factory already validates output (size + MP4 ftyp) and refunds on failure. Only borrow specific FFmpeg/asset-validation refinements if a concrete gap is found.

candidates.name: Graft
candidates.capability: Name maps to 5+ unrelated projects: Delavalom/graft (Go agent framework), graft-org/graft (legacy tool contracts), AEndrix03/Graft (local semantic cache), odvcencio/graft (structural VCS), wavect Graft (repo-map, MIT npm).
useful_patterns: repo-as-linked-markdown + per-symbol code graph (the repo-map variant is relevant to codebase intelligence)
candidates.rationale: Repository identity is ambiguous. Per directive: do NOT integrate. If the intended target is the repo-map variant, it overlaps with codebase-memory-mcp (already covered).

candidates.name: Harness Engineering / agent harness
candidates.capability: 'Harness' is ambiguous (harness.io CI/CD company vs the general 'agent harness' testing/repair pattern).
candidates.rationale: No single repo to integrate. Getszy ALREADY implements this pattern (agent_evidence ledger + next_strategy + agent_llm bounded rounds/attempts). Treat as validation of existing design; refine, do not replace.

candidates.name: Scientific / Research Agent skills
candidates.capability: Name maps to many possible projects (scientific-paper agents, research-agent skills).
candidates.rationale: Ambiguous identity. Learn the research-lifecycle discipline and wrap Getszy's existing agent_research tools with it; no source integration.

candidates.name: Diagram-generation skills
useful_patterns: derive diagrams from real repository evidence
rejected_patterns: inventing architecture not present in the repo
candidates.rationale: Getszy can emit mermaid natively at near-zero cost. Derive diagrams from the structural repo-map (codebase intelligence) so architecture is evidence-based, not invented.
